> **Companion PR:** vllm-project/ci-infra#820 (dual-mode pipeline generator — must merge together or with ci-infra first)

Currently on CI and deployment, we have:

- **Too many image tiers.** The old pipeline had six distinct image layers (base, ci_base, CI image, wheels, test, smoke), each driven by a separate script with its own cache keys and metadata handoffs. Adding or debugging any step required understanding all six.
- **CI and release were disconnected.** CI built images via `ci-bake-rocm.sh`; release rebuilt from scratch using a separate pipeline. The bytes shipped to users were never the bytes tested on GPUs.
- **Thousands of lines of bash nobody could operate.** `ci-bake-rocm.sh` alone was 2,784 lines. The ROCm build/deploy surface totalled ~12,000 lines of shell with no human able to read, modify or debug it under pressure.

In this PR, the purpose is to have:

**Two image tiers, one Dockerfile, one HCL, three readable scripts.**

1. **Stack** (`rocm/vllm-ci:stack-rocm-<Ks>`) — base OS + ROCm + PyTorch. Built only when `docker/Dockerfile.rocm_base` or `tools/vllm-rocm/therock_wheels.py` changes (content key `Ks`). Pushed once; reused by every subsequent build.
2. **Per-commit** (`rocm/vllm-ci:build-<build-id>`) — vLLM compiled on top of the stack. The runtime key `Kr` (hash of `Ks` + Dockerfile above the marker + pip requirement files) gates whether the runtime layer is rebuilt. A Python-only commit reuses the runtime; a requirements bump rebuilds it; a csrc-only change rebuilds neither.

**One shared `docker/Dockerfile.rocm`.** A named BuildKit context (`stack`) is injected by the bake HCL, so the same Dockerfile builds on any stack without duplication.

**One static `docker/docker-bake-rocm.hcl`** replaces the dynamically generated `docker/ci-rocm.hcl`. All parameterisation is through HCL `variable` blocks from environment variables. Targets cover all combinations: stack, runtime, CI test, csrc, wheels, release.

**`build.sh` (240 lines) replaces ~5,000 lines of shell scripts.** Six modes: `keys`, `base`, `ci`, `check`, `csrc`, `release`. Each mode is a self-contained named section, readable end-to-end.

**Release promotes the CI digest — no rebuild.** `build.sh release` reads the exact digest of the CI-tested image and reuses it. A non-blocking `rel-csrc` step compiles csrc for all 9 GPU arches (gfx90a/942/950/1100/1101/1200/1201/1150/1151); because csrc inputs rarely change (~8% of commits), this is almost always a BuildKit cache hit.

**`rocm-release.yaml` (53 lines) + `publish.sh` (200 lines) handle release publishing.** A trigger-only `amd-release` Buildkite pipeline uploads `rocm-release.yaml` once per main commit. `publish.sh` copies digests via `imagetools create` to ECR, Docker Hub, and S3 — no Docker build, no layer transfer.

**ROCm 7.2 (apt) deprecated.** All `rocm_72` stack plumbing removed: `Dockerfile.rocm_72_base`, `stack-rocm_72` bake target, `rocm72-check-amd` CI step, ROCm 7.2 release pipeline group. TheRock 10 (`rocm`) is the only supported stack.

**ci-infra is dual-mode.** The pipeline generator checks for `.buildkite/scripts/rocm/build.sh` in the vLLM checkout. Present → new pipeline renders. Absent (old checkouts, forks) → existing pipeline unchanged.

**Image pre-warming.** Runtime tags are content-keyed (`runtime-rocm-<Kr>`). A cluster cron job can pre-pull by checking tag presence before pulling, avoiding the 200-node simultaneous pull on rare runtime rebuilds.

### What is preserved

- **Step key `image-build-amd`** — unchanged. All 229 GPU test steps continue to depend on it.
- **`SETUP_STEP_KEYS = {"refresh-rocm-base-amd", "pre-commit"}`**
- **Smoke tests** — `openai-smoke` and `test-smoke` stages in `Dockerfile.rocm`; `rel-gpu` GPU smoke on `amd_mi250_1` in `rocm-release.yaml`.
- **Process lifecycle** — `run-amd-test.sh` handles: `CONTAINER_TIMEOUT_S` wall-clock timeout (`timeout --foreground`), structured `[amd-ci-teardown]` lifecycle log events, exit-code propagation, DPX GPU partition lock, HF mount check, NFS xet redirect, GPU preflight, diagnostics bundle on failure.
- **Nightly tags** (`vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly*`, `base-nightly*`), S3 wheels per main commit, perf-eval ECR image, credential boundaries.
- **AITER nightly** — ci-infra old-layout path unchanged; new-layout renders the AITER overlay step via `AITER_SPEC`.

### Net change

39 files, **+1,894 / −8,922** vs `origin/main`.

| File | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `docker/Dockerfile.rocm` | 1,016 | 483 |
| `docker/Dockerfile.rocm_base` | 476 | 404 |
| `docker/docker-bake-rocm.hcl` | 143 | 118 |
| `.buildkite/scripts/rocm/build.sh` | — | 240 (new) |
| `.buildkite/scripts/rocm/publish.sh` | — | 200 (new) |
| `.buildkite/rocm-release.yaml` | — | 53 (new) |
| `tests/tools/test_rocm_build.py` | — | 49 (new) |
| `docker/context/base-wheels/.keep` | — | new (gfx1250 COPY fix) |
| `.buildkite/scripts/hardware_ci/run-amd-test.sh` | 1,813 | 182 |
| `.buildkite/hardware_tests/amd.yaml` | 88 | 47 |
| `.buildkite/release-pipeline.yaml` | 1,055 | ~820 |
| `docker/Dockerfile.rocm_72_base` | 388 | deleted |
| `docker/ci-rocm.hcl` | 411 | deleted |
| `.buildkite/scripts/ci-bake-rocm.sh` | 2,784 | deleted |
| ROCm `rocm/*.sh` scripts (8 files) | ~1,600 | deleted |
| ROCm release scripts (3 files) | ~300 | deleted |
| `requirements/build/rocm.txt` | 19 | deleted |

**ROCm build/deploy surface after this PR:** 1 Dockerfile (483 lines), 1 HCL (118 lines), 3 bash scripts (build 240, publish 200, run-amd-test 182 = 622 lines total).

### Follow-up infra tasks

- **`amd-release` Buildkite pipeline** — create trigger-only pipeline in vllm-project's org with `ROCM_STACK` env var.
- **`rocm/vllm-ci-pr` Docker Hub repo** — create with push access for the `amd-cpu` agent token.
- **`amd-cpu-pr` queue split** — run PR builds on separate hosts with their own Hub token. One comment in `build.sh` marks the boundary.
- **Cluster pre-warm cron** — pre-pull `rocm/vllm-ci:runtime-rocm-<Kr>` on CI nodes with a tag-presence check.
- **Hub tag retention** — content-addressed tags; define an expiry window.
- **gfx1250 Dockerfiles** (`Dockerfile.rocm_gfx1250`, `Dockerfile.rocm_base_gfx1250`) — kept as-is, not wired into CI or release; needs owner sign-off before removal.

---

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to draft this change. Every line was reviewed by the submitter.

@@ -0,0 +1,72 @@
+---
+name: model-microbenchmark
+description: Time a vLLM model's forward pass on exact batch shapes (decode, prefill, chunked prefill, prefix hit, spec-decode verify, or mixes) with `vllm bench forward`, single-GPU or DP/TP/EP across nodes. Use for per-step model latency, layout/parallelism comparisons, and checking a model-level optimization. Not for single kernels (use kernel-microbenchmark) or end-to-end serving (use `vllm bench serve`).
+---
+
+# Model Microbenchmark (`vllm bench forward`)
+
+Builds the batch without the scheduler, runs it through MRV2's real
+`execute_model`, and times the forward as a one-shot CUDA graph (prefill
+included). Sampling, the speculator, and CPU step overhead are excluded, so
+expect results somewhat below a serving step.
+
+## Usage
+
+```bash
+vllm bench forward --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
+  --case decode=64*1@8192 --case prefill=8192 --case mix=4096,32*1@8192
+
+# DP/TP/EP: one process per GPU (multi-node: add --nnodes/--node-rank/--master-addr)
+torchrun --nproc-per-node=4 -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main bench forward \
+  --model ... -dp 4 --enable-expert-parallel --case decode=128*1@100000
+```
+
+Requests: `[N*]Q[@K][c][:D]`, comma-separated, per DP rank.
+
+| Form | Meaning |
+| --- | --- |
+| `8192` | fresh prefill, 8192 tokens |
+| `32*1@8192` | 32 decodes, KV length 8192 (KV length **includes** the query) |
+| `4@4096:3` | spec-decode verify, 3 draft tokens |
+| `2048@10240` | prefill after an 8192-token prefix-cache hit |
+| `2048@10240c` | chunked prefill: the prefix came from earlier chunks |
+
+Hit vs chunk only differs on models with SWA bounded replay (DSV4.1): a hit
+also recomputes the last window (128 tokens) of the prefix.
+
+Or `--shapes file.json|yaml`:
+`{"cases": [{"name": ..., "requests": [{"query_len", "kv_len", "num_draft_tokens", "chunked", "count"}]}]}`.
+
+Key flags (plus all `EngineArgs`):
+
+- `--kv-len-jitter 0.5` (default): prefixes drawn within ±50%, same on every
+  DP rank, capped at `max_model_len`. Use `0` for exact lengths.
+- `--routing auto|real|balanced`: `auto` = balanced with dummy weights.
+- `--iters 20 --samples 5`, `--output-json out.json` (per-rank latency stats,
+  `samples_us`, graph-vs-eager check).
+- Defaults: `--load-format dummy`, prefix caching off, no torch.compile.
+
+Read `median_us` (each replay is already the max over ranks).
+
+## Caveats
+
+- **Dummy weights lie for data-dependent kernels.** Dummy gates route every
+  token to the same experts (hence balanced routing). Cross-check suspicious
+  kernels with real weights.
+- **torch.compile models (e.g. Qwen3/3.5) look slow**: no compile here. Use
+  them for correctness only; trust perf for models under `vllm/models/`.
+- `sample spread > 0.5%` warns of unstable timing. DSV4.1 DEP prefill is
+  inherently ~0.5–1% (MegaMoE cross-rank sync, host engram reads).
+- `graph_vs_eager` may be nonzero for small batches where models branch on
+  `is_current_stream_capturing()`; that's expected, not a bug.
+- KV cache is zero-initialized (`--kv-init zeros`); random KV was within 3%.
+- Uniform DP only: every rank gets the same case; no idle ranks.
+- CUDA only: it hangs on ROCm (untested cause: likely the in-graph timing
+  events).
+- Large prefills/prefix hits need room: raise `--max-num-batched-tokens` /
+  `--max-model-len` / `--gpu-memory-utilization` if build fails on KV blocks.
+- Startup cost is JIT/autotune, not the bench: install FlashInfer jit-cache
+  and cubin; DeepGEMM warmup is skipped (each case's eager pass compiles its
+  own shapes).
+- To compare against serving decode: `vllm bench latency` with 65- vs
+  1-token outputs, divided by 64, with a FULL decode graph.

+# ROCm release mode for one stack, uploaded by the trigger-only `amd-release` pipeline, which
+# release-pipeline.yaml triggers with ROCM_STACK=rocm. Builds and GPU-smokes
+# rocm/vllm-ci:<stack>-<commit>{,-wheels,-base}; publishing happens back on AWS (rocm/publish.sh).
+env:
+  ROCM_CI_REPO: rocm/vllm-ci
+
+steps:
+  - label: ":rocm: ${ROCM_STACK:?set by the release trigger} stack + runtime"
+    key: rel-base
+    agents: {queue: amd-cpu}
+    command: bash .buildkite/scripts/rocm/build.sh ${ROCM_STACK} base
+    timeout_in_minutes: 540
+    concurrency: 1
+    concurrency_group: "vllm/rocm/base/${ROCM_STACK}/rocm/vllm-ci/$BUILDKITE_PULL_REQUEST/$BUILDKITE_BRANCH" # = main CI's
+
+  - label: ":rocm: ${ROCM_STACK} all-arch csrc"
+    key: rel-csrc
+    depends_on: rel-base
+    agents: {queue: amd-cpu}
+    command: bash .buildkite/scripts/rocm/build.sh ${ROCM_STACK} csrc
+    timeout_in_minutes: 300
+    concurrency: 1
+    concurrency_group: "vllm/rocm/csrc/${ROCM_STACK}"
+
+  - label: ":rocm: ${ROCM_STACK} release image + wheels"
+    key: rel-build
+    depends_on: rel-csrc
+    agents: {queue: amd-cpu}
+    command: bash .buildkite/scripts/rocm/build.sh ${ROCM_STACK} release
+    timeout_in_minutes: 120
+
+  # The only GPU run of the exact shipped image; its failure keeps it out of ECR, Docker Hub and S3.
+  - label: ":rocm: ${ROCM_STACK} GPU smoke (MI300)"
+    key: rel-gpu
+    depends_on: rel-build
+    agents: {queue: amd_mi250_1}
+    command: vllm bench throughput --model facebook/opt-125m --input-len 32 --output-len 32 --num-prompts 8
+    timeout_in_minutes: 30
+    plugins:
+      - kubernetes:
+          podSpecPatch:
+            automountServiceAccountToken: false
+            securityContext: {seccompProfile: {type: RuntimeDefault}}
+            imagePullSecrets: [{name: docker-config}]
+            containers:
+              - name: container-0
+                image: rocm/vllm-ci:${ROCM_STACK}-$BUILDKITE_COMMIT
+                imagePullPolicy: Always
+                securityContext: {allowPrivilegeEscalation: false, capabilities: {add: [IPC_LOCK]}}
+                resources: {limits: {amd.com/gpu: "1"}, requests: {amd.com/gpu: "1"}}
+                env: [{name: HF_HOME, value: /home/buildkite-agent/huggingface}]  # node's HF cache
+                volumeMounts: [{name: devshm, mountPath: /dev/shm}]
+            volumes: [{name: devshm, emptyDir: {medium: Memory, sizeLimit: 16Gi}}]

-#!/usr/bin/env bash
-# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

-#
-# Cache helper for ROCm base wheels
-#
-# This script manages caching of pre-built ROCm base wheels (torch, triton, etc.)
-# to avoid rebuilding them when Dockerfile.rocm_base hasn't changed.
-#
-# Usage:
-#   cache-rocm-base-wheels.sh check    - Check if cache exists, outputs "hit" or "miss"
-#   cache-rocm-base-wheels.sh upload   - Upload wheels to cache
-#   cache-rocm-base-wheels.sh download - Download wheels from cache
-#   cache-rocm-base-wheels.sh key      - Output the cache key
-#
-# Environment variables:
-#   S3_BUCKET          - S3 bucket name (default: vllm-wheels)
-#
-# Note: ROCm version is determined by BASE_IMAGE in Dockerfile.rocm_base,
-#       so changes to ROCm version are captured by the Dockerfile hash.
-
-set -euo pipefail
-
-BUCKET="${S3_BUCKET:-vllm-wheels}"
-DOCKERFILE="docker/Dockerfile.rocm_base"
-CACHE_PREFIX="rocm/cache"
-
-# Generate hash from Dockerfile content + build args
-generate_cache_key() {
-    # Include Dockerfile content
-    if [[ ! -f "$DOCKERFILE" ]]; then
-        echo "ERROR: Dockerfile not found: $DOCKERFILE" >&2
-        exit 1
-    fi
-    local dockerfile_hash=$(sha256sum "$DOCKERFILE" | cut -c1-16)
-
-    echo "${dockerfile_hash}"
-}
-
-CACHE_KEY=$(generate_cache_key)
-CACHE_PATH="s3://${BUCKET}/${CACHE_PREFIX}/${CACHE_KEY}/"
-
-case "${1:-}" in
-    check)
-        echo "Checking cache for key: ${CACHE_KEY}" >&2
-        echo "Cache path: ${CACHE_PATH}" >&2
-
-        # Check if cache exists by listing objects
-        # We look for at least one .whl file
-        echo "Running: aws s3 ls ${CACHE_PATH}" >&2
-        S3_OUTPUT=$(aws s3 ls "${CACHE_PATH}" 2>&1) || true
-        echo "S3 ls output:" >&2
-        echo "$S3_OUTPUT" | head -5 >&2
-
-        if echo "$S3_OUTPUT" | grep -q "\.whl"; then
-            echo "hit"
-        else
-            echo "miss"
-        fi
-        ;;
-
-    upload)
-        echo "========================================"
-        echo "Uploading wheels to cache"
-        echo "========================================"
-        echo "Cache key: ${CACHE_KEY}"
-        echo "Cache path: ${CACHE_PATH}"
-        echo ""
-
-        if [[ ! -d "artifacts/rocm-base-wheels" ]]; then
-            echo "ERROR: artifacts/rocm-base-wheels directory not found" >&2
-            exit 1
-        fi
-
-        WHEEL_COUNT=$(find artifacts/rocm-base-wheels -maxdepth 1 -name '*.whl' 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
-        if [[ "$WHEEL_COUNT" -eq 0 ]]; then
-            echo "ERROR: No wheels found in artifacts/rocm-base-wheels/" >&2
-            exit 1
-        fi
-
-        echo "Uploading $WHEEL_COUNT wheels..."
-        aws s3 cp --recursive artifacts/rocm-base-wheels/ "${CACHE_PATH}"
-
-        echo ""
-        echo "Cache upload complete!"
-        echo "========================================"
-        ;;
-
-    download)
-        echo "========================================"
-        echo "Downloading wheels from cache"
-        echo "========================================"
-        echo "Cache key: ${CACHE_KEY}"
-        echo "Cache path: ${CACHE_PATH}"
-        echo ""
-        mkdir -p artifacts/rocm-base-wheels
-        
-        # Use sync with include/exclude to only download .whl files
-        aws s3 sync "${CACHE_PATH}" artifacts/rocm-base-wheels/ \
-            --exclude "*" \
-            --include "*.whl"
-        
-        echo ""
-        echo "Downloaded wheels:"
-        find artifacts/rocm-base-wheels -maxdepth 1 -name '*.whl' -exec ls -lh {} \;
-        WHEEL_COUNT=$(find artifacts/rocm-base-wheels -maxdepth 1 -name '*.whl' 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
-        echo ""
-        echo "Total: $WHEEL_COUNT wheels"
-        echo "========================================"
-        ;;
-
-    key)
-        echo "${CACHE_KEY}"
-        ;;
-
-    path)
-        echo "${CACHE_PATH}"
-        ;;
-
-    *)
-        echo "Usage: $0 {check|upload|download|key|path}" >&2
-        echo "" >&2
-        echo "Commands:" >&2
-        echo "  check    - Check if cache exists, outputs 'hit' or 'miss'" >&2
-        echo "  upload   - Upload wheels from artifacts/rocm-base-wheels/ to cache" >&2
-        echo "  download - Download wheels from cache to artifacts/rocm-base-wheels/" >&2
-        echo "  key      - Output the cache key" >&2
-        echo "  path     - Output the full S3 cache path" >&2
-        exit 1
-        ;;

-# When commands are passed through Buildkite -> shell -> $* -> bash -c,

-# This function detects unquoted expressions after -m/-k and re-quotes them

-#   - test path (contains '/')

-# unquoted since they have no spaces and work fine.

-# through untouched to avoid double-quoting well-formed shell fragments.

-# double-quotes stripped by the calling shell (see header comment).

+#!/bin/bash
+# Install the AITER nightly wheel over this build's ci_base.
+#
+# Runs in CI when AITER_NIGHTLY=1, once the stock ci_base it builds on is
+# published. In order:
+#   1. Select the newest nightly wheel that fits the stock ci_base
+#      (select_aiter_nightly_wheel.py, beside this script, run inside that image)
+#   2. Build a new image: pip install that wheel over the stock ci_base
+#   3. Push the new image as this build's ci_base-build tag, replacing the stock
+#      one, so later steps and native jobs use it; record its digest
+#
+# Buildkite meta-data, a key-value store shared by every job in this build:
+#   reads   rocm-ci-base-image       the stock ci_base
+#   r/w     aiter-nightly-wheel-url  the wheel step 1 chose; a retry reads it
+#                                    back and installs that same wheel
+#   writes  aiter-nightly-ci-base    the new image as tag@digest; the vLLM
+#                                    image build uses it as its ci_base
+#
+# Exit status:
+#   10  no wheel fits this ci_base
+#   11  the wheel does not install
+#   Anything else is unexpected and passed through as is.
+#   Buildkite retries this step once on exit status 1 or 2, which it treats as
+#   transient Docker/registry failures (amd_infra_retry in the template).
+#   10 and 11 sit outside that range: they are real AITER failures, and a retry
+#   would only fail the same way.
+
+set -euo pipefail
+
+SELECT_WHEEL="$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/select_aiter_nightly_wheel.py"
+BUILD_TAG="rocm/vllm-dev:ci_base-build-${BUILDKITE_BUILD_ID:?BUILDKITE_BUILD_ID is required}"
+
+# Scratch space for the build context and captured errors. The trap deletes it
+# however the script exits: success, fail, or set -e.
+scratch="$(mktemp -d)"
+trap 'rm -rf "${scratch}"' EXIT
+errors="${scratch}/errors"
+
+fail() {
+    local status="$1" title="$2" detail="$3"
+    echo "+++ :x: AITER nightly: ${title}"
+    echo "${detail}" >&2
+    # shellcheck disable=SC2016 # the backticks are a literal markdown fence
+    printf ':x: **AITER nightly: %s**\n\n```\n%s\n```\n' "${title}" "${detail}" \
+        | buildkite-agent annotate --style error --context aiter-nightly
+    exit "${status}"
+}
+
+# Set by ensure-ci-base-amd; this step's depends_on guarantees it is there.
+ci_base="$(buildkite-agent meta-data get rocm-ci-base-image)"
+# Set below on the first attempt. Meta-data is per build, so a retry reuses
+# that wheel, not a newer nightly.
+pinned="$(buildkite-agent meta-data get aiter-nightly-wheel-url --default "")"
+
+echo "--- :docker: Pulling ${ci_base}"
+docker pull "${ci_base}"
+
+echo "--- :mag: Selecting the AITER nightly for ${ci_base}"
+set +e
+out="$(docker run --rm -i --entrypoint python3 "${ci_base}" \
+    -P - ${pinned:+--wheel-url "${pinned}"} \
+    < "${SELECT_WHEEL}" 2> "${errors}")"
+status=$?
+set -e
+cat "${errors}" >&2
+case "${status}" in
+    0) ;;
+    10) fail 10 "no wheel for this image" "${out}" ;;
+    *) fail "${status}" "could not select a wheel" "$(tail -n 20 "${errors}")" ;;
+esac
+# The first line is the wheel's URL; the rest, the annotation naming it.
+wheel_url="$(head -n 1 <<< "${out}")"
+note="$(tail -n +2 <<< "${out}")"
+buildkite-agent meta-data set aiter-nightly-wheel-url "${wheel_url}"
+
+cat > "${scratch}/Dockerfile" <<'EOF'
+ARG CI_BASE_IMAGE
+FROM ${CI_BASE_IMAGE}
+ARG AITER_WHEEL_URL
+RUN python3 -m pip install --no-cache-dir "$AITER_WHEEL_URL"
+EOF
+
+echo "--- :docker: Installing ${wheel_url##*/}"
+if ! docker buildx build \
+    --builder default \
+    --provenance=false \
+    --progress plain \
+    --build-arg "CI_BASE_IMAGE=${ci_base}" \
+    --build-arg "AITER_WHEEL_URL=${wheel_url}" \
+    -t "${BUILD_TAG}" \
+    "${scratch}"; then
+    fail 11 "the wheel does not install" \
+        "Installing ${wheel_url##*/} over ${ci_base} failed; see this step's log."
+fi
+
+docker push "${BUILD_TAG}"
+# Handed off as tag@digest: build-test-image.sh rejects a ci_base that is not
+# digest-pinned.
+digest="$(docker buildx imagetools inspect "${BUILD_TAG}" | awk '$1 == "Digest:" { print $2; exit }')"
+if [[ ! "${digest}" =~ ^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]]; then
+    echo "Could not resolve the pushed digest of ${BUILD_TAG}" >&2
+    exit 1
+fi
+# The vLLM image build uses this as its ci_base.
+buildkite-agent meta-data set aiter-nightly-ci-base "${BUILD_TAG}@${digest}"
+# The annotation starts with :warning: when the wheel is stale.
+style=info
+if [[ "${note}" == :warning:* ]]; then
+    style=warning
+fi
+echo "${note}" | buildkite-agent annotate --style "${style}" --context aiter-nightly
+echo "--- :white_check_mark: ${BUILD_TAG}@${digest}"

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+#
+# Build and promote ROCm images via docker/docker-bake-rocm.hcl.
+# Pushes only to $ROCM_CI_REPO (set by ci-infra) and its BuildKit cache.
+#
+# Usage: build.sh <stack> <mode>
+#
+# Modes:
+#   keys     Print current Ks/Kr keys and whether their images exist (on-call debug).
+#   base     Ensure stack + runtime images exist; write their refs to Buildkite metadata.
+#   ci       Build and push this build's per-commit test image.
+#   check    Build + smoke (no push) — pre-merge signal gated on rocm-relevant files.
+#   csrc     All-arch csrc compile into the BuildKit cache (release, serialized per stack).
+#   release  Full release image + wheels from the CI-tested layers.
+#
+# Stack: rocm (TheRock ROCm 10). Force a stack rebuild: bump ARG REFRESH
+#        in docker/Dockerfile.rocm_base.
+#
+# Trust: ci-infra sets ROCM_CI_REPO.
+#   Trusted main builds: rocm/vllm-ci
+#   PR / fork builds:    rocm/vllm-ci-pr  (PR-namespaced tags, separate cache)
+set -euo pipefail
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Arguments and trust
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+STACK=$1
+MODE=$2
+REPO=${ROCM_CI_REPO:?ROCM_CI_REPO must be set by ci-infra}
+
+export STACK PUSH=true
+export CACHE=rocm/vllm-ci-cache        # every build reads the trusted layer cache
+export CACHE_TO=rocm/vllm-ci-cache:latest  # main builds also write it
+
+# PR builds write to a per-PR cache and prefix their image tags.
+PFX=""
+if [[ $REPO != rocm/vllm-ci ]]; then
+  PFX="pr${BUILDKITE_PULL_REQUEST:-local}-"
+  CACHE_TO=$REPO:cache-pr${BUILDKITE_PULL_REQUEST:-local}-
+fi
+
+# Stack Dockerfile — literal path used by ci-infra ci_selector (images.py).
+case $STACK in
+  rocm) SDF=docker/Dockerfile.rocm_base ;;
+  *) echo "Unknown stack: $STACK" >&2; exit 2 ;;
+esac
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# BuildKit builder
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Prefer the host buildkitd (it has its own GC policy and cache). Fall back
+# to a docker-container builder if no socket is present.
+if ! docker buildx inspect vllm-rocm >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+  if [[ -S /run/buildkit/buildkitd.sock ]]; then
+    drv=(--driver remote unix:///run/buildkit/buildkitd.sock)
+  else
+    drv=(--driver docker-container \
+      ${BUILDKITD_CONFIG:+--buildkitd-config "$BUILDKITD_CONFIG"})
+  fi
+  # || inspect: tolerate a race where another job created it between the check and create.
+  docker buildx create --name vllm-rocm "${drv[@]}" >/dev/null \
+    || docker buildx inspect vllm-rocm >/dev/null
+fi
+export BUILDX_BUILDER=vllm-rocm
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Git tags — required by the version stage
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# setuptools_scm needs a reachable v* tag. Agents clone shallow and tagless;
+# --force updates tags that moved (e.g. a re-tag after a release candidate).
+git fetch -q --force --tags --filter=tree:0 origin
+git describe --tags --match 'v[0-9]*' >/dev/null 2>&1 \
+  || git fetch -q --unshallow --filter=tree:0 origin
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Helper functions
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+# digest <ref>
+#   Print the manifest digest of <ref>.
+#   Returns 1 (without error output) if the tag does not exist.
+#   Any other registry error is fatal: kill $$ instead of exit 1 because
+#   this function is called from $() subshells where exit only exits the subshell.
+digest() {
+  local out
+  out=$(docker buildx imagetools inspect "$1" \
+          --format '{{.Manifest.Digest}}' 2>&1) && { echo "$out"; return 0; }
+  grep -qiE 'not found|manifest unknown' <<<"$out" && return 1
+  echo "registry error for $1: $out" >&2
+  kill $$
+}
+
+# label <ref> <key>  — read one image label
+label() { docker buildx imagetools inspect "$1" \
+            --format "{{index .Image.Config.Labels \"$2\"}}"; }
+
+# bake <targets...>  — invoke docker buildx bake with the project HCL
+bake()   { docker buildx bake -f docker/docker-bake-rocm.hcl "$@"; }
+
+# meta <get|set> <key> [value]  — Buildkite build metadata
+meta()   { buildkite-agent meta-data "$@"; }
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Content keys
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Ks (stack key): hash of the stack Dockerfile + therock_wheels.py.
+#   A Ks cache miss triggers a full stack rebuild (hours).
+# Kr (runtime key): Ks + the portion of Dockerfile.rocm above the per-commit
+#   marker + all pip requirement files.
+#   A Kr cache miss triggers a runtime rebuild (minutes).
+
+_trw=$( [[ $STACK == rocm ]] && echo tools/vllm-rocm/therock_wheels.py || true )
+Ks=$(git ls-tree HEAD -- "$SDF" $_trw | sha256sum | cut -c1-16)
+Kr=$(
+  {
+    echo "$Ks"
+    sed '/^# ==== per-commit stages/q' docker/Dockerfile.rocm
+    git ls-tree HEAD -- \
+      requirements/common.txt \
+      requirements/rocm.txt \
+      requirements/test/rocm.txt \
+      tools/install_torchcodec_rocm.sh
+  } | sha256sum | cut -c1-16
+)
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# ensure <bake-target> <tag-suffix> [<sibling-suffix>]
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Resolve a content-keyed image without building if it already exists.
+# Resolution order:
+#   1. Trusted registry (rocm/vllm-ci:<tag>) — safe for any build to reuse.
+#   2. This repo's own tag ($REPO:$PFX<tag>) — PR builds write here.
+#   3. Neither found: build via bake and push.
+# A <sibling-suffix> means the image only counts as present when the sibling
+# tag also exists (used by stack: must have both the image and -wheels).
+ensure() {
+  local target=$1 tag=$2 sibling=${3:-} ref digest_val
+
+  for ref in "rocm/vllm-ci:$tag" "$REPO:$PFX$tag"; do
+    digest_val=$(digest "$ref") \
+      && { [[ -z $sibling ]] || digest "$ref$sibling" >/dev/null; } \
+      && { echo "$ref@$digest_val"; return 0; }
+  done
+
+  # Neither copy found — build and push.
+  TAG=$REPO:$PFX$tag bake "$target" >&2
+  digest_val=$(digest "$REPO:$PFX$tag") && echo "$REPO:$PFX$tag@$digest_val"
+}
+
+# load — read stack/runtime refs from Buildkite metadata (written by base mode).
+load() {
+  STACK_IMAGE=$(meta get "rocm-$STACK-stack")
+  STACK_WHEELS=$(meta get "rocm-$STACK-stack-wheels")
+  RUNTIME=$(meta get "rocm-$STACK-runtime")
+  export STACK_IMAGE STACK_WHEELS RUNTIME
+}
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Mode dispatch
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+case $MODE in
+
+  keys)
+    # Print current content keys and registry status (useful for on-call triage).
+    for t in "stack-$STACK-$Ks" "runtime-$STACK-$Kr"; do
+      echo "$t  $(digest "rocm/vllm-ci:$t" 2>/dev/null || echo MISSING)"
+    done
+    ;;
+
+  base)
+    # Ensure the stack and runtime images exist; record their digests in metadata
+    # so subsequent ci / release modes can pull them without re-resolving.
+    STACK_IMAGE=$(ensure stack-$STACK "stack-$STACK-$Ks" -wheels)
+    export STACK_IMAGE
+    RUNTIME=$(ensure runtime "runtime-$STACK-$Kr")
+    wheels_ref=${STACK_IMAGE%@*}-wheels
+
+    meta set "rocm-$STACK-stack"        "$STACK_IMAGE"
+    meta set "rocm-$STACK-runtime"      "$RUNTIME"
+    meta set "rocm-$STACK-stack-wheels" "$wheels_ref@$(digest "$wheels_ref")"
+    ;;
+
+  ci)
+    # Build and push the per-commit test image for GPU test steps.
+    load
+    export TAG=$REPO:build-$BUILDKITE_BUILD_ID
+    # AITER nightly injects a specific AITER wheel via AITER_SPEC.
+    [[ ${AITER_NIGHTLY:-0} != 1 ]] \
+      || export AITER_SPEC=${AITER_SPEC:?AITER_SPEC must be set by the nightly schedule}
+    bake ci
+    ;;
+
+  check)
+    # Smoke-build for a file-gated pre-merge check (no push).
+    load
+    PUSH=false bake test-smoke
+    ;;
+
+  csrc)
+    # Compile csrc for all 9 release arches into the BuildKit cache.
+    # Run non-blocking and serialized per stack; almost always a cache hit.
+    load
+    PUSH=false bake csrc-all
+    ;;
+
+  release)
+    # Build and push the final release image + wheels from the CI-tested layers.
+    # Trusted builds only: the released image carries the rocm/vllm-ci namespace.
+    [[ $REPO == rocm/vllm-ci ]] \
+      || { echo "release mode is for trusted builds only" >&2; exit 1; }
+    load
+    export TAG=rocm/vllm-ci:$STACK-$BUILDKITE_COMMIT
+
+    # Resolve the vLLM version from the commit (setuptools_scm).
+    PUSH=false bake version
+    VLLM_VERSION=$(cat .rocm-version/vllm-version.txt)
+    export VLLM_VERSION
+
+    # Skip if this exact version was already released (handles rc → final re-tags).
+    if digest "$TAG" >/dev/null \
+        && [[ $(label "$TAG" org.opencontainers.image.version) == "$VLLM_VERSION" ]]; then
+      echo "Release image $TAG already exists with version $VLLM_VERSION — skipping." >&2
+      exit 0
+    fi
+
+    # Build wheels first (csrc layer is a cache hit from rel-csrc in almost all cases).
+    bake wheels openai-smoke
+    # Alias the runtime as the -base tag (the base-nightly consumer reference).
+    docker buildx imagetools create -t "$TAG-base" "$RUNTIME"
+    # Push the vllm-openai tag last — its presence marks the set as complete.
+    bake vllm-openai
+    ;;
+
+  *)
+    echo "Unknown mode: $MODE" >&2
+    exit 2
+    ;;
+esac

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+#
+# Promote ROCm release artifacts without rebuilding anything.
+# All source images were built and GPU-smoked by the amd-release pipeline;
+# this script only copies digests and uploads wheels.
+#
+# Usage: publish.sh <stack> <mode>
+#
+# Modes:
+#   wheels   Extract the vLLM wheel from the -wheels image and upload to S3.
+#   images   Copy the release image and its runtime base to ECR.
+#            With NIGHTLY=1, also push the nightly tags to Docker Hub.
+#
+# Required environment variables:
+#   BUILDKITE_COMMIT   — the commit being released
+#
+# Optional:
+#   ECR            — ECR repository prefix (default: public.ecr.aws/q9t5s3a7/vllm-release-repo)
+#   HUB            — Docker Hub repo for nightly images (default: vllm/vllm-openai-rocm)
+#   NIGHTLY        — set to 1 to push nightly Hub tags (default: 0)
+#   DOCKERHUB_USERNAME — Hub username for cleanup script (default: vllmbot)
+set -euo pipefail
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Arguments
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+STACK=$1
+MODE=$2
+COMMIT=${BUILDKITE_COMMIT:?BUILDKITE_COMMIT must be set}
+
+SRC=rocm/vllm-ci:${STACK}-${COMMIT}
+ECR=${ECR:-public.ecr.aws/q9t5s3a7/vllm-release-repo}
+HUB=${HUB:-vllm/vllm-openai-rocm}
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Helper functions
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+# pin <ref>  — resolve <ref> to a pinned ref@digest (resolves once, stable for the rest of the script)
+pin() { echo "$1@$(docker buildx imagetools inspect "$1" --format '{{.Manifest.Digest}}')"; }
+
+# variant <ref>  — read the ai.vllm.rocm.variant image label
+variant() {
+  docker buildx imagetools inspect "$1" \
+    --format '{{index .Image.Config.Labels "ai.vllm.rocm.variant"}}'
+}
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Resolve source image refs (done once; images step uses them too)
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+IMG=$(pin "$SRC")
+V=$(variant "$IMG")      # e.g. rocm100 — used in S3 paths, ECR tags and Hub tags
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Mode dispatch
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+case $MODE in
+
+  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
+  wheels)
+  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
+  # Extract the vLLM wheel from the content-keyed -wheels image and upload it
+  # to S3 so users can pip-install it directly.
+  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+    WHEELS_IMG=$(pin "$SRC-wheels")
+
+    # Export wheel files out of the scratch image into ./dist/
+    rm -rf dist
+    echo "FROM $WHEELS_IMG" | docker buildx build -q -o dist -
+
+    # Sanity: the wheel's variant suffix must match the stack label.
+    # (setup.py's rocm_version_to_variant produces e.g. rocm100 for 10.0.x)
+    actual_variant=$(basename dist/vllm-*.whl | grep -oE 'rocm[0-9]+' | tail -1)
+    [[ $actual_variant == "$V" ]] \
+      || { echo "Wheel variant $actual_variant != image variant $V" >&2; exit 1; }
+
+    bash .buildkite/scripts/upload-rocm-wheels.sh "$STACK" dist
+
+    # Buildkite annotation: pip install + direct S3 download commands.
+    WHL_URL="https://wheels.vllm.ai/rocm/$COMMIT/$V"
+    buildkite-agent annotate --style success --context "rocm-$STACK-wheels" << EOF
+## :package: ROCm \`$V\` wheels published
+
+| | |
+|---|---|
+| **Variant** | \`$V\` |
+| **Commit**  | \`$COMMIT\` |
+| **Branch**  | \`${BUILDKITE_BRANCH:-?}\` |
+
+### Install (this commit)
+\`\`\`bash
+pip install vllm --extra-index-url $WHL_URL
+\`\`\`
+
+### Install (latest nightly)
+\`\`\`bash
+pip install vllm --extra-index-url https://wheels.vllm.ai/rocm/nightly/$V
+\`\`\`
+
+### Download wheels directly
+\`\`\`bash
+aws s3 ls  s3://vllm-wheels/rocm/$COMMIT/$V/
+aws s3 cp  --recursive --include "*.whl" s3://vllm-wheels/rocm/$COMMIT/$V/ .
+\`\`\`
+EOF
+    ;;
+
+  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
+  images)
+  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
+  # Copy the release image and its runtime base to ECR.
+  # With NIGHTLY=1, also tag them on Docker Hub and prune old nightly tags.
+  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+    RT=$(pin "$SRC-base")    # runtime base alias (published as base-nightly*)
+
+    # --- ECR -----------------------------------------------------------------
+    aws ecr-public get-login-password --region us-east-1 \
+      | docker login -u AWS --password-stdin "${ECR%%/*}"
+
+    docker buildx imagetools create -t "$ECR:$COMMIT-$V"       "$IMG"
+    docker buildx imagetools create -t "$ECR:$COMMIT-$V-base"  "$RT"
+
+    # Write variant to Buildkite metadata so downstream steps
+    # (root-index generation, publish-release-images.sh) can read it.
+    buildkite-agent meta-data set "rocm-$STACK-variant" "$V"
+
+    ECR_IMG="$ECR:$COMMIT-$V"
+    ECR_BASE="$ECR:$COMMIT-$V-base"
+
+    # --- Non-nightly annotation ----------------------------------------------
+    if [[ ${NIGHTLY:-0} != 1 ]]; then
+      buildkite-agent annotate --style success --context "rocm-$STACK-images" << EOF
+## :docker: ROCm \`$V\` images published to ECR
+
+| | |
+|---|---|
+| **Variant** | \`$V\` |
+| **Commit**  | \`$COMMIT\` |
+| **ECR image** | \`$ECR_IMG\` |
+| **ECR base**  | \`$ECR_BASE\` |
+
+\`\`\`bash
+docker pull $ECR_IMG
+\`\`\`
+EOF
+      exit 0
+    fi
+
+    # --- Nightly: Docker Hub -------------------------------------------------
+    export DOCKERHUB_USERNAME=${DOCKERHUB_USERNAME:-vllmbot}
+
+    # The default stack (rocm) owns the unqualified :nightly / :base-nightly tags.
+    # All stacks own the variant-qualified :nightly-<variant> tags.
+    suffixes=("-$V")
+    [[ $STACK == rocm ]] && suffixes+=("")
+
+    hub_tags=""
+    for sfx in "${suffixes[@]}"; do
+      docker buildx imagetools create \
+        -t "$HUB:nightly$sfx" -t "$HUB:nightly$sfx-$COMMIT" "$IMG"
+      docker buildx imagetools create \
+        -t "$HUB:base-nightly$sfx" -t "$HUB:base-nightly$sfx-$COMMIT" "$RT"
+      hub_tags="$hub_tags \`$HUB:nightly$sfx\` \`$HUB:nightly$sfx-$COMMIT\`"
+    done
+
+    # Prune old nightly tags (keep last 14 builds per tag family).
+    clean=.buildkite/scripts/cleanup-nightly-builds.sh
+    bash "$clean" "nightly-$V-"      "$HUB"
+    bash "$clean" "base-nightly-$V-" "$HUB"
+    if [[ $STACK == rocm ]]; then
+      bash "$clean" "nightly-"      "$HUB" "nightly-rocm"
+      bash "$clean" "base-nightly-" "$HUB" "base-nightly-rocm"
+    fi
+
+    buildkite-agent annotate --style success --context "rocm-$STACK-images" << EOF
+## :docker: ROCm \`$V\` nightly images published
+
+| | |
+|---|---|
+| **Variant**   | \`$V\` |
+| **Commit**    | \`$COMMIT\` |
+| **ECR image** | \`$ECR_IMG\` |
+| **ECR base**  | \`$ECR_BASE\` |
+| **Docker Hub** |$hub_tags |
+
+\`\`\`bash
+docker pull $HUB:nightly-$V
+\`\`\`
+EOF
+    ;;
+

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Select the AITER nightly wheel for a vLLM ROCm image.
+
+aiter-nightly-overlay.sh runs this inside the stock ci_base, so it reads that
+image's ROCm, torch and Python. It prints the wheel's URL, then the Buildkite
+annotation naming it.
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import datetime
+import importlib.metadata
+import os
+import sys
+import urllib.request
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from html.parser import HTMLParser
+from pathlib import Path
+from urllib.parse import unquote, urldefrag, urljoin
+
+import regex as re
+
+INDEX_URL = "https://rocm.frameworks-nightlies.amd.com/whl-multi-arch/amd-aiter/"
+AITER_COMMIT_URL = "https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/commit/"
+STALE_AFTER = datetime.timedelta(days=1)
+
+# Example:
+#   amd_aiter-0.1.25+rocm7.2.3.torch2.12.ae984f5.d20261008-cp312-cp312-linux_x86_64.whl
+# is AITER main at commit ae984f5, built 2026-10-08, for ROCm 7.2.3, torch 2.12
+# and Python 3.12. 0.1.25 is a guess at the next release, not a real one.
+WHEEL_NAME = re.compile(
+    r"^amd_aiter-(?P<base_version>[^+-]+)\+(?P<local>[^-]+)"
+    r"-(?P<python>cp\d+)-(?P=python)-linux_x86_64\.whl$"
+)
+ROCM_FIELD = re.compile(r"(?:^|\.)rocm(\d+(?:\.\d+)*)(?:a\d+)?(?=\.|$)")
+TORCH_FIELD = re.compile(r"(?:^|\.)torch(\d+\.\d+)(?=\.|$)")
+COMMIT_AND_DATE_FIELD = re.compile(r"(?:^|\.)([0-9a-f]{7,40})\.d(\d{8})(?=\.|$)")
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class Wheel:
+    """An AITER nightly wheel, read from its filename (see WHEEL_NAME)."""
+
+    filename: str
+    url: str
+    version: str
+    base_version: str
+    rocm: str
+    torch: str
+    commit: str
+    build_date: datetime.date
+    python: str
+
+
+class _LinkParser(HTMLParser):
+    """Collects every link on the index page, which lists one per wheel."""
+
+    def __init__(self):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.hrefs: list[str] = []
+
+    def handle_starttag(self, tag, attrs):
+        if tag == "a":
+            self.hrefs.extend(
+                value for name, value in attrs if name == "href" and value
+            )
+
+
+def wheel_from_url(url: str) -> Wheel | None:
+    """The AITER nightly wheel an absolute URL points at, if it is one."""
+    filename = unquote(urldefrag(url).url.rsplit("/", 1)[-1])
+    match = WHEEL_NAME.match(filename)
+    if not match:
+        return None
+    local = match["local"]
+    rocm, torch, build = (
+        field.search(local)
+        for field in (ROCM_FIELD, TORCH_FIELD, COMMIT_AND_DATE_FIELD)
+    )
+    if not (rocm and torch and build):
+        return None
+    return Wheel(
+        filename=filename,
+        url=url,
+        version=f"{match['base_version']}+{local}",
+        base_version=match["base_version"],
+        rocm=rocm[1],
+        torch=torch[1],
+        commit=build[1],
+        build_date=datetime.datetime.strptime(build[2], "%Y%m%d").date(),
+        python=match["python"],
+    )
+
+
+def parse_index(html: str, index_url: str) -> list[Wheel]:
+    """Every AITER nightly wheel linked from the index page, a plain HTML list
+    of links, one per file (the format pip reads)."""
+    parser = _LinkParser()
+    parser.feed(html)
+    wheels = (wheel_from_url(urljoin(index_url, href)) for href in parser.hrefs)
+    return [wheel for wheel in wheels if wheel]
+
+
+def rocm_version() -> str:
+    """This image's ROCm version; ROCm 10+ ships as the `rocm` pip SDK."""
+    try:
+        return importlib.metadata.version("rocm")
+    except importlib.metadata.PackageNotFoundError:
+        # No pip SDK: fall back to older ROCm releases, which install to ROCM_PATH.
+        rocm_path = Path(os.environ.get("ROCM_PATH", "/opt/rocm"))
+        return (rocm_path / ".info" / "version").read_text()
+
+
+def rocm_release(version: str) -> str:
+    """`7.2.3-49` or `10.0.0a20261001` -> `7.2.3` or `10.0.0`, as wheel names
+    spell it."""
+    match = re.match(r"\d+(?:\.\d+)*", version.strip())
+    if not match:
+        raise ValueError(f"Unrecognised ROCm version: {version!r}")
+    return match.group(0)
+
+
+def torch_release(version: str) -> str:
+    """`2.12.0a0+git6bbd260` -> `2.12`, as wheel names spell it."""
+    match = re.match(r"\d+\.\d+", version)
+    if not match:
+        raise ValueError(f"Unrecognised torch version: {version!r}")
+    return match.group(0)
+
+
+def python_tag(version_info: tuple[int, int]) -> str:
+    """(3, 12) -> `cp312`, as wheel names spell it."""
+    return f"cp{version_info[0]}{version_info[1]}"
+
+
+def _base_version_key(wheel: Wheel) -> tuple[int, ...]:
+    """`0.1.25` -> (0, 1, 25), so versions sort as numbers: 0.1.10 > 0.1.9."""
+    return tuple(int(part) for part in re.findall(r"\d+", wheel.base_version))
+
+
+def _label(rocm: str, torch: str, python: str) -> str:
+    """`rocm7.2.3/torch2.12/cp312`, for messages."""
+    return f"rocm{rocm}/torch{torch}/{python}"
+
+
+def select_wheel(wheels: list[Wheel], rocm: str, torch: str, python: str) -> Wheel:
+    """Newest build for this ROCm, torch and Python, by date: version labels lag.
+
+    Two builds with the same date and version: whichever the index lists first.
+    """
+    target = (rocm, torch, python)
+    matching = [w for w in wheels if (w.rocm, w.torch, w.python) == target]
+    if not matching:
+        available = sorted({_label(w.rocm, w.torch, w.python) for w in wheels})
+        raise LookupError(
+            f"No AITER nightly for {_label(*target)}. "
+            f"Available: {', '.join(available) or 'none'}"
+        )
+    return max(matching, key=lambda w: (w.build_date, _base_version_key(w)))
+
+
+def fetch(url: str) -> str:
+    """GET url as text. A failure exits 1, so Buildkite retries the step."""
+    with urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=60) as response:
+        return response.read().decode()
+
+
+def annotation(wheel: Wheel, today: datetime.date) -> str:
+    """The Buildkite annotation naming the wheel this build tests.
+
+    Starts with :warning: if the wheel is stale; the overlay script styles it so.
+    """
+    age = today - wheel.build_date
+    stale = (
+        f":warning: **AITER nightly is {age.days} days old**: "
+        f"no newer build has been published for "
+        f"{_label(wheel.rocm, wheel.torch, wheel.python)}.\n\n"
+        if age > STALE_AFTER
+        else ""
+    )
+    return stale + (
+        f":crescent_moon: **AITER nightly**: main at "
+        f"[`{wheel.commit}`]({AITER_COMMIT_URL}{wheel.commit}), "
+        f"built {wheel.build_date.isoformat()} for torch {wheel.torch} "
+        f"(`{wheel.version}`)"
+    )
+
+
+class NoWheel(Exception):
+    """No wheel fits this image's ROCm, torch and Python. Exit 10."""
+
+
+def _image_wheel(wheel_url: str) -> Wheel:
+    """The wheel at wheel_url, if it fits this image's ROCm, torch and Python."""
+    wheel = wheel_from_url(wheel_url)
+    if not wheel:
+        raise NoWheel(f"Not an AITER nightly wheel: {wheel_url}")
+    return _for_image([wheel])
+
+
+def _image() -> tuple[str, str, str]:
+    """This image's ROCm, torch and Python, as wheel names spell them."""
+    try:
+        rocm = rocm_release(rocm_version())
+    except (OSError, ValueError) as error:
+        raise NoWheel(f"Cannot read this image's ROCm version: {error}") from error
+    try:
+        torch = torch_release(importlib.metadata.version("torch"))
+    except (importlib.metadata.PackageNotFoundError, ValueError) as error:
+        raise NoWheel(f"Cannot read this image's torch version: {error}") from error
+    return rocm, torch, python_tag(sys.version_info[:2])
+
+
+def _for_image(wheels: list[Wheel]) -> Wheel:
+    """The newest of wheels for the image this runs in."""
+    try:
+        return select_wheel(wheels, *_image())
+    except LookupError as error:
+        raise NoWheel(str(error)) from error
+
+
+def select(index_url: str, wheel_url: str = "") -> Wheel:
+    """The wheel to install: wheel_url on a retry, else the newest.
+
+    However old the newest is, it is tested; the annotation shows its build date.
+    """
+    if wheel_url:
+        return _image_wheel(wheel_url)
+    return _for_image(parse_index(fetch(index_url), index_url))
+
+
+def _today() -> datetime.date:
+    """Today in UTC; a function so tests can set the date."""
+    return datetime.datetime.now(datetime.UTC).date()
+
+
+# Not 1 or 2, which Buildkite retries; see aiter-nightly-overlay.sh.
+EXIT_NO_WHEEL = 10
+
+
+def main(argv=None) -> int:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--index-url", default=INDEX_URL)
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--wheel-url", default="", help="a retry's earlier choice; skips the index"
+    )
+    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
+    try:
+        wheel = select(args.index_url, args.wheel_url)
+    except NoWheel as error:
+        print(error)
+        return EXIT_NO_WHEEL
+    print(wheel.url)
+    print(annotation(wheel, _today()))
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main())

+"""Compare in-tree vs AITER sparse-indexer prefill top-k at GLM-5.3-Flash shapes.
+
+Example:
+    .venv/bin/python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_sparse_indexer_topk_prefill.py \
+        --num-rows 1024 --num-cols 131072 --topk 512
+
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import os
+import time
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm import _custom_ops  # noqa: F401
+from vllm._aiter_ops import rocm_aiter_ops
+
+
+def _make_inputs(num_rows, num_cols, causal, device):
+    logits = torch.randn(num_rows, num_cols, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
+    row_starts = torch.zeros(num_rows, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+    if causal:
+        ramp = torch.arange(1, num_rows + 1, device=device, dtype=torch.float32)
+        row_ends = (ramp * (num_cols / num_rows)).ceil().to(torch.int32)
+    else:
+        row_ends = torch.full((num_rows,), num_cols, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+    return logits, row_starts, row_ends
+
+
+def _time(fn, iters, warmup):
+    for _ in range(warmup):
+        fn()
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    start = time.perf_counter()
+    for _ in range(iters):
+        fn()
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    return (time.perf_counter() - start) / iters * 1e3
+
+
+def _selected_set(indices, row_starts):
+    valid = indices >= 0
+    return [set(r[m].tolist()) for r, m in zip(indices.cpu(), valid.cpu())]
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+    parser.add_argument("--num-rows", type=int, default=1024)
+    parser.add_argument("--num-cols", type=int, default=131072)
+    parser.add_argument("--topk", type=int, default=512)
+    parser.add_argument("--causal", action="store_true")
+    parser.add_argument("--iters", type=int, default=20)
+    parser.add_argument("--warmup", type=int, default=5)
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+
+    device = torch.device("cuda")
+    logits, row_starts, row_ends = _make_inputs(
+        args.num_rows, args.num_cols, args.causal, device
+    )
+    print(
+        f"rows={args.num_rows} cols={args.num_cols} k={args.topk} "
+        f"causal={args.causal} logits={logits.numel() * 4 / 2**20:.0f} MiB "
+        f"path={os.environ.get('TOPK_FORCE_PATH', 'auto')}"
+    )
+
+    native = torch.empty(args.num_rows, args.topk, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+
+    def run_native():
+        torch.ops._C.top_k_per_row_prefill(
+            logits,
+            row_starts,
+            row_ends,
+            native,
+            args.num_rows,
+            logits.stride(0),
+            logits.stride(1),
+            args.topk,
+        )
+
+    native_ms = _time(run_native, args.iters, args.warmup)
+    print(f"in-tree  topKPerRowPrefill : {native_ms:8.3f} ms")
+
+    if not rocm_aiter_ops.is_indexer_top_k_enabled():
+        print(
+            "AITER path unavailable: requires ROCm gfx950 with AITER installed "
+            "and VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1"
+        )
+        return
+
+    from vllm.v1.attention.ops.rocm_aiter_mla_sparse import (
+        _launch_aiter_top_k_per_row_prefill,
+    )
+
+    aiter_out = torch.empty(args.num_rows, args.topk, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+
+    def run_aiter():
+        _launch_aiter_top_k_per_row_prefill(
+            logits, row_starts, row_ends, aiter_out, args.topk
+        )
+
+    try:
+        aiter_ms = _time(run_aiter, args.iters, args.warmup)
+    except Exception as exc:
+        print(f"AITER path failed: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}")
+        return
+    print(f"AITER    top_k_per_row_prefill: {aiter_ms:8.3f} ms")
+    print(f"speedup  : {native_ms / aiter_ms:.2f}x")
+
+    ref = _selected_set(native, row_starts)
+    got = _selected_set(aiter_out, row_starts)
+    mismatched = sum(1 for a, b in zip(ref, got) if a != b)
+    worst = max((len(a ^ b) for a, b in zip(ref, got)), default=0)
+    print(f"rows differing: {mismatched}/{args.num_rows} (worst sym-diff {worst})")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+#pragma once
+
+#include <torch/all.h>
+
+// Need a special dispatch case macro since we will nest the FP8 dispatch.
+// Instead of the usual 'scalar_t', this names the dispatched type 'fp8_t'.
+#define AT_DISPATCH_FP8_CASE(enum_type, ...) \
+  AT_PRIVATE_CASE_TYPE_USING_HINT(enum_type, fp8_t, __VA_ARGS__)
+
+// ROCm devices might use either fn or fnuz, so set up dispatch table for both.
+// A host-based check at runtime will create a preferred FP8 type for ROCm
+// such that the correct kernel is dispatched.
+#define VLLM_DISPATCH_CASE_FP8_TYPES(...)                          \
+  AT_DISPATCH_FP8_CASE(at::ScalarType::Float8_e4m3fn, __VA_ARGS__) \
+  AT_DISPATCH_FP8_CASE(at::ScalarType::Float8_e4m3fnuz, __VA_ARGS__)
+
+// When using this dispatch macro, the type is 'fp8_t' not 'scalar_t'.
+// See AT_DISPATCH_FP8_CASE above.
+#define VLLM_DISPATCH_FP8_TYPES(TYPE, NAME, ...) \
+  AT_DISPATCH_SWITCH(TYPE, NAME, VLLM_DISPATCH_CASE_FP8_TYPES(__VA_ARGS__))

+# Expert substitution (MoNE)
+
+[Mixture of Novices and Experts (MoNE)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.00390)
+prunes MoE layers by replacing redundant experts with "novices" that return a
+constant vector. vLLM loads the retained experts into compact weights and adds
+the novices' output separately, so pruned experts use no MLP weight memory and
+no MoE backend needs to know about them.
+
+## Checkpoint format
+
+The checkpoint keeps the original architecture. `config.json` lists the
+substituted experts of each decoder layer:
+
+```json
+{
+  "architectures": ["DeepseekV2ForCausalLM"],
+  "n_routed_experts": 64,
+  "approximate_experts": {
+    "1": [1, 6, 8, 12],
+    "2": [0, 3, 17, 40]
+  }
+}
+```
+
+For VLMs, `approximate_experts` may live on the text config. Retained experts
+keep their logical checkpoint names. Each substituted expert stores one
+`[hidden_size]` tensor instead of its MLP:
+
+```text
+model.layers.1.mlp.experts.0.gate_proj.weight
+model.layers.1.mlp.experts.1.approx_value
+```
+
+Alternatively, `compression_config.transform_config.expert_substitution`
+declares the same information with explicitly named constant tensors:
+
+```json
+{
+  "compression_config": {
+    "transform_config": {
+      "expert_substitution": {
+        "version": 1,
+        "router_semantics": {
+          "preserve_logical_expert_ids": true,
+          "preserve_router_weights": true,
+          "renormalize_after_substitution": false
+        },
+        "targets": {
+          "model.layers.1.mlp.experts": {
+            "num_logical_experts": 64,
+            "weight_layout": "compact_retained_experts",
+            "replacements": {
+              "1": {
+                "format": "constant-v1",
+                "tensors": {"value": "model.layers.1.mlp.expert_replacements.1.value"}
+              }
+            }
+          }
+        }
+      }
+    }
+  }
+}
+```
+
+Only the values shown for `version`, `router_semantics`, `weight_layout`, and
+`format` are supported. Each target path must contain exactly one layer index.
+This form is not yet accepted alongside compressed-tensors quantization, whose
+`transform_config` schema does not include `expert_substitution`.
+
+## Semantics
+
+For a substituted expert `j` with constant `v_j` and router weight `w_j(x)`,
+the expert contributes `w_j(x) v_j`. Routing is unchanged: router weights are
+neither renormalized nor redistributed to retained experts.
+
+## Execution
+
+`FusedMoEFactory` matches each MoE layer to `approximate_experts` by the layer
+index in its prefix and, for a match, builds `SubstitutedRoutedExperts`, which:
+
+1. allocates weights only for retained experts, in ascending logical order;
+2. after routing, sums `w_j(x) v_j` over substituted routes in FP32;
+3. rewrites substituted routes as zero-weight routes to physical expert 0 and
+   retained routes as compact physical IDs, preserving the `[num_tokens, top_k]`
+   contract of every decomposed backend;
+4. adds the constant output on one tensor-parallel rank, before the partial
+   outputs are all-reduced.
+
+Zero-weight routes may schedule some unnecessary GEMM work; the memory savings
+are unaffected. Monolithic backends route internally and are not selected.
+
+## Weight loading
+
+Retained experts are loaded through the standard expert mapping by logical ID
+and placed in their compact row. Substituted IDs map to no local row, the same
+way expert parallelism skips non-local experts.
+
+Constant tensors are consumed at the model's `load_weights` boundary, so
+initial loading and direct weight updates share one path. `approx_value` tensors of
+layers that the model does not build (other pipeline stages, MTP layers) are
+passed through to the model's loader, which skips them like any other weight
+it does not own. Explicitly named constants are always consumed, and dropped
+when their layer is built elsewhere. Loading fails if a local substituted
+expert has no constant.
+
+Direct `load_weights` updates may change individual constants. Layerwise
+reloads (`reload_weights` in checkpoint format) are rejected, and the model
+keeps its previous weights.
+
+## Supported configurations
+
+- Models whose MoE layers use `FusedMoEFactory` with the default
+  `RoutedExperts`, and whose MoE prefix contains exactly one layer index.
+- Unquantized experts.
+- Tensor and pipeline parallelism, including MTP draft models.
+- Any decomposed MoE backend.
+
+Expert and data parallelism, EPLB, MoE LoRA, fused shared experts, quantized
+experts, and routed input/output transforms are rejected at initialization.
+Deferred MoE finalize and layerwise weight reloads are rejected when used.

+## Info Metric Labels
+
+The connector publishes one Prometheus gauge, `vllm:kv_offload_config_info`, and always sets it to 1. The labels hold static facts of the offloading configuration, so a user reads the resolved numbers instead of the launch flags. The gauge appears from the first scheduler step, so an idle engine exposes no series. Each engine reports its own configuration, and not the instance total.
+
+The gauge holds one series for each configuration that the manager reports. A manager that holds one configuration gives one series. A manager that holds several adds a label of its own, which tells the series apart.
+
+| Label | Declared by | Meaning | Notes |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| `tier` | `TieringOffloadingSpec` | The tier that this series reports. | `<index>:<type>`. Index `0` is the CPU primary tier, and a secondary tier index starts at 1. `<type>` is the `type` key of the tier config, such as `1:fs`. |
+| `cpu_num_chunks` | `CPUOffloadingSpec` or `TieringOffloadingSpec` | Chunk slots in the CPU tier. | Chunks, not GPU blocks. `cpu_bytes_to_use` divided by the bytes of one chunk. |
+
+The spec declares the label names in the API server process, and the manager fills the values in the engine process. The names of every series bind once, at the declaration. A label that one series owns reads empty on every other series.
+
+`CPUOffloadingSpec` publishes `cpu_num_chunks` on its one series. `TieringOffloadingSpec` publishes it on the `0:primary` series. For a worked example of a secondary tier, the `example` tier publishes one label, `example_info`.
+
+A manager adds a label with `config_info_keys()` of its spec and `config_info()` of its own class. A name that a manager fills and the spec does not declare is dropped, and the engine log then holds one warning line.

+## ModelOpt block codecs
+
+ModelOpt mixed-precision checkpoints select block codecs through the
+`quantization_config.quantized_layers` entries in `config.json`. Each entry
+declares `quant_algo`, `group_size`, `block_payload_bytes`, and `packing="ggml"`:
+
+| `quant_algo` | `group_size` | `block_payload_bytes` |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `IQ2_XS` | 256 | 74 |
+| `IQ2_XXS` | 256 | 66 |
+| `Q8_0` | 32 | 34 |
+
+Serialized matrices have uint8 shape `[N, K/group_size, block_payload_bytes]`.
+Dense preparation rearranges the encoded blocks without expanding the matrix
+to BF16. Routed experts use bias-free SiLU or non-gated ReLU²; tensor-parallel
+shards must preserve whole blocks and satisfy the kernel's alignment constraints.
+Only Q8_0 supports packed embedding lookup.
+
+Quantized normalization weights and other packed vectors are not supported.
+Store normalization weights as ordinary floating-point tensors and omit their
+entries from `quantization_config.quantized_layers`.
+
+Dense, embedding, and expert matrices remain packed. Their execution uses BF16
+activations without activation quantization. Prepare the kernels and workspaces
+before CUDA graph capture.

+## Monitoring
+
+When `watermark_config` is set, the Prometheus counter
+`vllm:watermark_requests_total` counts finished requests by `status`:
+
+- `watermarked`: the request was sampled with the watermark switched on.
+- `skipped`: the request asked for the watermark (omitted or `true`) but could
+  not use it, such as `temperature=0` and trace replay requests. A beam search
+  request that asks for the watermark runs without it and logs a warning. Its
+  beam steps count as `not_watermarked`, not `skipped`.
+- `not_watermarked`: all other finished requests. This includes explicit
+  opt-outs, pooling requests, and the internal requests of beam search (one
+  per beam step), generative scoring and language detection.
+
+Each finished request has exactly one status, so the sum over `status` equals
+`vllm:request_success_total` on the same instance. Requests that the client
+aborts are in neither counter. The counter does not exist without
+`watermark_config`. With `n > 1`, each sequence counts once. In a
+disaggregated prefill/decode deployment, both instances count a request: sum
+over decode instances only. For streaming input, the first input chunk sets
+the status.
+
+The status is per request, not per token. A `watermarked` request can contain
+tokens without the watermark: accepted draft tokens with
+`allow_target_only_watermarking`, tokens whose context repeats
+(`deduplicate_contexts`), the first `context_width` generated tokens with
+`deduplicate_contexts: "all"`, and tokens that a grammar forces.

+### Fixed-length late chunking
+
+Late chunking encodes the full input before averaging contextual token representations within each chunk. The chunk means pass through the model's embedding head, including its projection and optional normalization.
+
+This mode is currently available through the offline `LLM.encode` API for plain-text input. With an instance configured for `token_embed`, enable it per request:
+
+```python
+from vllm import PoolingParams
+from vllm.pooling_params import LateChunkingParams
+
+outputs = llm.encode(
+    [document],
+    pooling_task="token_embed",
+    pooling_params=PoolingParams(
+        late_chunking_params=LateChunkingParams(chunk_size=256)
+    ),
+)
+vectors = outputs[0].outputs.data  # [num_chunks, embedding_dimension]
+chunks = outputs[0].late_chunking.chunks
+```
+
+For `N` model-input tokens and chunk size `C`, the output contains `ceil(N / C)` vectors. The last chunk uses its actual length. Special tokens and instruction prefixes count toward both chunk boundaries and means. Omitting `late_chunking_params` preserves ordinary token embeddings.
+
+Each vector row corresponds to one entry in `chunks`. Its `token_range` and `char_range` are zero-based, half-open ranges. Character ranges index the submitted Python string; use `document[start:end]` to retrieve the source text. A chunk containing only special tokens has `char_range=None`.
+
+Use nonempty text within the model's context window and a fast tokenizer that provides aligned source offsets. Input truncation, explicit padding and renderer text normalization are not supported. The custom document/query outputs of `JinaForRanking` are also unsupported. Late chunking does not extend the model's context window or reduce its attention computation.
+
+The [offline example](../../../examples/pooling/token_embed/late_chunking_offline.py) loads an E5 model and prints the vector shape, token ranges and source excerpts for two documents:
+
+```bash
+python examples/pooling/token_embed/late_chunking_offline.py --chunk-size 16
+```
+

+# Structured Decisions Models
+
+Structured Decisions Models (aka JEV Models) map inputs directly to predefined
+options or categories and return probabilities and confidence scores, commonly
+used for classification and routing.
+
+## Supported Models
+
+### Text-only Models
+
+| Architecture              | ReadStrategy        | Task             | Head              | Example HF Models       |
+|---------------------------|---------------------|------------------|-------------------|-------------------------|
+| `ClefFlashForJointSchema` | `ClefFlashStrategy` | `token_classify` | `JointSchemaHead` | `Cloudflare/clef-flash` |
+| `Qwen3ForCausalLM`        | `NextTokenStrategy` | `generate`       | N/A               | `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, etc. |
+
+### Multimodal Models
+
+!!! note
+    For more information about multimodal models inputs, see [this page](./supported_models.md#list-of-multimodal-language-models).
+
+| Architecture                         | Inputs                              | ReadStrategy                   | Task             | Head              | Example HF Models                        |
+|--------------------------------------|-------------------------------------|--------------------------------|------------------|-------------------|------------------------------------------|
+| `ClefOmniForJointSchema`             | T + I + V                           | `JointSchemaStrategy`          | `token_classify` | `JointSchemaHead` | `Cloudflare/clef-omni`                   |
+| `D3ForSequenceClassification`        | T + I + V                           | `D3Strategy`                   | `classify`       | Linear (`score`)  | `vllm-sr/d3`, `vllm-sr/d3-mini`, etc.    |
+| `Lfm2VlForConditionalGeneration`     | T + I<sup>+</sup>                   | `LiquidStrategy`               | `generate`       | N/A               | `LiquidAI/d1-3B`                         |
+| `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration`    | T + I<sup>E+</sup> + V<sup>E+</sup> | `NextTokenStrategy`            | `generate`       | N/A               | `Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B`, etc.                |
+| `Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration` | T + I<sup>E+</sup> + V<sup>E+</sup> | `NextTokenStrategy`            | `generate`       | N/A               | `Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B`, etc.             |
+| `DiffusionGemmaForBlockDiffusion`    | T + I<sup>+</sup> + V<sup>+</sup>   | `DiffusionGemmaCanvasStrategy` | `generate`       | N/A               | `google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it`, etc. |
+
+## Online Serving
+
+### TypeSafe System One Endpoint
+
+The `/v1/systemone` endpoint answers a set of typed questions about a state and
+returns a probability for every allowed answer.
+
+The endpoint is available by default on generation models. Models without a
+supported read strategy return 501. Supported architectures require
+`--logprobs-mode raw_logprobs` or `processed_logprobs`, since `label_mass` needs
+log probabilities.
+
+#### How it works
+
+1. Each question is one read. The user message is the state, followed by the
+   question and its options with the type's labels, and an instruction to
+   answer with one label.
+2. The read is the reply's first token. Each label must be one token there,
+   or the request returns 400.
+3. The read returns the logprobs of that question's label tokens. Softmax over
+   the labels gives the answer's probabilities.
+
+Thinking is off unless `chat_template_kwargs` turns it on.
+
+Probabilities can differ between identical requests. They depend on which
+requests share a batch and on whether a read hits the prefix cache. Set
+`VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` for reads that repeat exactly, at a cost in
+throughput.
+
+Every read of a request starts with the state, so with
+`--enable-prefix-caching` the state is prefilled once and each further
+question prefills only its own text, then reads one token.
+
+#### Question types
+
+| type | criteria | answer |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `choice` | map of option name to a description or `null` | `choice`, `probabilities` by option name, `confidence` |
+| `noul` | `null`, or an object with optional `true` and `false` descriptions | `noul` (probability of yes), `probabilities`, `confidence` |
+| `score` | ordered list of level names | `score` (expected 0-indexed level), `legend`, `probabilities` by level index, `confidence` |
+
+A choice has at least one option, a score at least two levels. A question id
+is a non-empty string.
+
+#### Example
+
+```bash
+curl -s http://localhost:8000/v1/systemone \
+  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
+  -d '{
+    "model": "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B",
+    "state": {"ticket": "My card was charged twice for one order."},
+    "questions": {
+      "team": {
+        "type": "choice",
+        "instructions": "Which team should handle this ticket?",
+        "criteria": {
+          "billing": "payments and refunds",
+          "shipping": "deliveries",
+          "security": "account access"
+        }
+      },
+      "urgent": {
+        "type": "noul",
+        "instructions": "Does the customer need a reply within the hour?",
+        "criteria": {"true": "the account is locked or money is moving"}
+      },
+      "tone": {
+        "type": "score",
+        "instructions": "How upset is the customer?",
+        "criteria": ["calm", "annoyed", "furious"]
+      }
+    },
+    "chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": false}
+  }'
+```
+
+Response, with probabilities that depend on the model:
+
+```json
+{
+  "id": "decision-...",
+  "object": "structured_decision",
+  "created": 1790000000,
+  "model": "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B",
+  "answers": {
+    "team": {
+      "type": "choice",
+      "choice": "billing",
+      "probabilities": {"billing": 0.97, "shipping": 0.01, "security": 0.02},
+      "confidence": 0.90
+    },
+    "urgent": {
+      "type": "noul",
+      "noul": 0.02,
+      "probabilities": {"yes": 0.02, "no": 0.98},
+      "confidence": 0.95
+    },
+    "tone": {
+      "type": "score",
+      "score": 0.6,
+      "legend": {"0": "calm", "1": "annoyed", "2": "furious"},
+      "probabilities": {"0": 0.7, "1": 0.2, "2": 0.1},
+      "confidence": 0.65
+    }
+  },
+  "usage": {"input_tokens": 142, "output_tokens": 3},
+  "diagnostics": {
+    "team": {"label_mass": 0.93, "argmax_is_label": true},
+    "urgent": {"label_mass": 0.98, "argmax_is_label": true},
+    "tone": {"label_mass": 0.91, "argmax_is_label": true}
+  }
+}
+```
+
+`diagnostics.label_mass` is the probability the model put on the labels across
+its whole vocabulary. A low value means most of the probability went to tokens
+that are not labels. `confidence` is the chosen option's probability over the
+whole vocabulary: its share of the labels times `label_mass`.
+
+#### Labels
+
+Labels follow the type: a `choice` labels its options `A` to `Z` in the order
+the request lists them, a `noul` labels its options `yes` and `no`, and a
+`score` labels its levels `0` to `9`, so a level's label is its score.
+
+#### Limits
+
+| limit | value |
+| --- | --- |
+| questions per request | 64 |
+| options per `choice` | 26 |
+| levels per `score` | 10 |
+
+#### Request fields
+
+| field | meaning |
+| --- | --- |
+| `state` | what the questions are about: a string, or JSON that is sent as its JSON text |
+| `questions` | question id to `{type, instructions, criteria}`, asked in this order |
+| `instructions` | optional context placed ahead of the questions |
+| `chat_template_kwargs` | passed to the chat template, for example `{"enable_thinking": false}` |
+| `cache_salt` | optional [prefix-cache salt](../usage/security.md#cache-salting) applied to every question |
+| `images`, `audio`, `videos` | optional media URLs or data URLs, for models that take them ([Clef-Flash](#clef-flash), images/video; [Clef-Omni](#clef-omni); [Decision 3.0](#decision-30), images/video; [Liquid d1](#liquid-d1), images only) |
+
+A question with any field other than `type`, `instructions` and `criteria` is
+rejected with a 400.
+
+When [tracing](../../examples/observability/opentelemetry/README.md) is enabled
+with `--otlp-traces-endpoint`, the HTTP `traceparent` and `tracestate` headers are
+forwarded to every question's generation request.
+
+### OpenAI Decisions API
+
+vLLM provides a text-only implementation of OpenAI's
+[`POST /v1/decisions`](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/decisions)
+API. Start a supported model:
+
+```bash
+vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B
+```
+
+```python
+from openai import OpenAI
+
+client = OpenAI(base_url="http://localhost:8000/v1", api_key="EMPTY")
+decision = client.decisions.create(
+    model="Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B",
+    input="The package arrived with a broken screen.",
+    questions=[
+        {
+            "type": "predicate",
+            "name": "damaged",
+            "instructions": "Does the customer report a damaged item?",
+        },
+        {
+            "type": "choice",
+            "name": "department",
+            "instructions": "Which department should handle this complaint?",
+            "choices": [{"value": "returns"}, {"value": "billing"}],
+        },
+        {
+            "type": "score",
+            "instructions": "How severe is the damage?",
+            "levels": [{"label": "cosmetic"}, {"label": "broken"}],
+        },
+    ],
+)
+print(decision.answers)
+```
+
+Use OpenAI Python SDK 3.26.0 or newer for `client.decisions.create`.
+`input` accepts a string or an array of user messages with string content or
+`input_text` parts. Answers retain question order and echo `name`, including
+`null` for unnamed questions. Choice values preserve strings and booleans.
+Scores are probability-weighted averages of zero-based level indices.
+
+The request contract follows the OpenAI OpenAPI schemas retrieved on
+October 7, 2026. This MVP supports 1–64 questions, 2–26 choices, and 2–10 score
+levels. Upstream permits 200 questions and 255 choices; this backend returns
+a 400 when either model limit is exceeded.
+The optional `safety_identifier` is caller metadata, available in request
+body logging with `--enable-log-requests` and DEBUG logging; it does not
+authenticate callers.
+
+#### Implementation and limits
+
+This MVP uses the same label-reading backend as
+[structured decisions](structured_decisions_models.md). It supports generation
+architectures with a registered read strategy, including Qwen, DiffusionGemma,
+and Liquid d1; unsupported models return 501. Each question reads a model's
+label tokens. Usage reports the actual prompt and output tokens across these
+reads, including prefix-cache counters.
+
+Probabilities are normalized over the supplied options. `confidence` is the
+winning label's probability over the full vocabulary; it is not calibrated
+to OpenAI's models. Thinking is disabled for these reads.
+
+Image inputs, other message roles, tools, streaming, and per-question refusal
+scoring are outside this MVP. Unsupported request fields and input types are
+rejected. The `/v1/systemone` endpoint retains its existing request format and
+is available by default.
+
+## Examples
+
+### Clef-Flash
+
+[Clef-Flash](https://huggingface.co/Cloudflare/clef-flash) uses a Qwen3.5-9B
+backbone and a joint schema head to score all questions in one forward pass.
+vLLM detects the head and serves the checkpoint as a pooling model.
+
+```bash
+vllm serve Cloudflare/clef-flash --max-model-len 16384
+```
+
+Send requests to `/v1/systemone` using `state` and `questions`, as in the
+examples above. `choice`, `noul` and `score` questions are supported.
+
+- Text and JSON states use the checkpoint's fixed prompt. JSON is compact
+  with sorted keys. `instructions` returns 400; `chat_template_kwargs`
+  has no effect.
+- The state is truncated to fit 16,384 tokens, or `max_model_len` if smaller.
+  A schema that exceeds this bound returns 400.
+- `images` and `videos` are placed before the state. Videos are sampled at
+  2 fps and processed by the Qwen3.5 vision processor. Audio inputs return
+  400, and video soundtracks are ignored.
+- Each request performs one pooling read. `usage.input_tokens` counts the
+  prompt once, `output_tokens` is 0, and `label_mass` is 1.
+
+### Clef-Omni
+
+[Clef-Omni](https://huggingface.co/Cloudflare/clef-omni) is a decision model:
+a joint schema head on the Qwen3-Omni thinker scores every option of every
+question in one forward pass. vLLM serves it as a pooling model.
+
+```bash
+vllm serve Cloudflare/clef-omni
+```
+
+- A request is one read. The prompt is the one the checkpoint's
+  `joint_schema_model.py` builds: the state, then every question with its
+  options. A JSON state is written as compact JSON with sorted keys.
+- A state too long for the model is truncated to fit, as the reference does.
+  A request whose questions alone exceed 64,000 tokens, or `max_model_len`,
+  returns 400.
+- `instructions` returns 400, since the prompt is fixed. `chat_template_kwargs`
+  has no effect.

+  `output_tokens` is 0.

+  before the state, videos sampled at 2 fps, and a video's soundtrack heard
+  with it when every video has one. Audio clips cannot be sent together with
+  videos that have soundtracks.
+
+### Decision 3.0
+
+The Decision 3.0 models ([`vllm-sr/d3`](https://huggingface.co/vllm-sr/d3) and
+its smaller variants such as `vllm-sr/d3-mini` and `vllm-sr/d3-edge`) are a
+Qwen3.5 backbone with an answer-code readout: one forward pass per question,
+and the readout scores the question's options at the last token. vLLM detects
+the checkpoint's `decision_config.json` and serves it as a classification
+model.
+
+```bash
+vllm serve vllm-sr/d3
+```
+
+- Each question is one read of the prompt the checkpoint's `d3_format.py`
+  writes: the state, the question and one line per option under an answer
+  code. A question's probabilities are the softmax of its options' code
+  logits at the checkpoint's temperature, so picks and probabilities match
+  `model.system_one()`. `confidence` and `usage` follow the definitions on
+  this page instead.

+  and an empty state as `(empty)`.

+  checkpoint declares, so chunked prefill and prefix caching are off.

+  `chat_template_kwargs` has no effect.
+- `images` and `videos` are placed before the text, images read at up to
+  1.6 megapixels and videos at 2 fps, at most 32 frames of up to
+  0.2 megapixels each, as the checkpoint's runtime does. The media are read
+  once and shared by every question of the request.
+- `/classify` and `/pooling` return the raw logits of all 255 codes; only the
+  first codes, one per option, belong to a question.
+
+### Liquid d1
+
+[`LiquidAI/d1-3B`](https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/d1-3B) is LFM2.5-VL-3B
+post-trained to answer decisions as the first token of its reply. vLLM serves
+it as a generative model.
+
+```bash
+vllm serve LiquidAI/d1-3B
+```
+
+- The server writes the prompt and reads the label tokens the way the
+  `prompt.py` shipped with the checkpoint does, so picks and probabilities
+  match `model.system_one()`. `confidence` and `usage` follow the definitions
+  on this page instead.
+- A JSON state is written as indented JSON. A `null` state leaves the images,
+  or the question alone, as the prompt.
+- `images` are placed before the state and shrunk to at most 1024 x 1024
+  pixels, as the reference does.
+- A `choice` whose option names are all single letters is labeled with those
+  letters.
+- When each request carries one question over a state that changes from
+  request to request, `--no-enable-prefix-caching` lowers latency.
